tooltips.tco: Total Cost of Ownership = Total cost including purchase, maintenance, fuel/energy, insurance over entire lifetime.
tooltips.discountRate: Rate used to calculate present value of future flows. Typically 4-8% for business projects.
tooltips.minAutonomy: Minimum range required for your daily routes. Plan for a 20% margin for contingencies.

tooltips.loadProfile: Average vehicle load profile. Impacts energy consumption and battery wear.
tooltips.minTemperature: Minimum operating temperature. Batteries lose 15-25% range in cold weather (-10°C).
tooltips.tripType: Type of trips made. Urban: frequent stops, Peri-urban: mixed, Regional: inter-city, Long distance: highway.
tooltips.subsidies: Available incentives: Ecological bonus, Conversion premium, Regional grants, Tax depreciation.
tooltips.maintenance: EV maintenance costs typically 30-40% lower than diesel (fewer wear parts).
tooltips.vehiclePrice: Catalog price excluding tax. EVs are more expensive to purchase but cheaper to operate.
tooltips.h2Type: Hydrogen type strongly impacts CO₂ emissions. Green hydrogen (renewable electrolysis) emits 20x less than grey.

helpTraining.title: Help and method
helpTraining.subtitle: How H2Fleet turns your actual fleet into a costed replacement plan — and where the numbers come from.

disclaimer.title: Read before presenting a result
disclaimer.text: Results are planning estimates computed by the TCO engine from your fleet and a registry of sourced assumptions. Each value carries its source, verification date and a status (verified, estimate, to validate). Replace estimates with your own data (prices paid, quotes, confirmed subsidies) before any decision.

journey.title: The 7-step journey
journey.p1: Fleet: pick the project’s actual vehicles (from My fleet), their replacement year and target technology; sorting and bulk actions, target suggested by Feasibility.
journey.p2: Feasibility: electric and hydrogen verdict per vehicle, costed by the engine (discounted savings or extra cost, payback, CO₂ avoided, subsidies), with caveats (long-haul, off-road, H₂ refuelling).
journey.p3: Strategies: three strategies compared with the status quo, stress test, then “Apply this strategy to the plan” after a detailed confirmation; the retained strategy is recorded.
journey.p4: Plan: annual budget (investment, subsidies, remaining to finance, operations) and charging infrastructure per depot (chargers, power, phasing).
journey.p5: Financing: plan subsidies per vehicle, client-confirmed subsidies (priority), application tracking per program and the program registry with computed status.
journey.p6: Reports: council-ready PDF and Excel workbook, frozen at each generation (engine version and input fingerprint in the footer).
journey.p7: Tracking: actual vs planned (replacements marked completed with date, acquired vehicle and actual cost) and tasks tied to vehicles, years and subsidies.

method.title: The TCO method
method.p1: Reference (status quo): the same fleet replaced in the same years by equivalent new diesels. Savings are always measured against this reference.
method.p2: Year 0 = acquisition; operations at the end of years 1 to H (project horizon). Each vehicle enters the calculation in ITS replacement year.
method.p3: Nominal cash flows (inflation per item) discounted at the project’s nominal rate — rate and horizon are editable project parameters.
method.p4: Taxes: the non-recoverable share of GST/QST depends on the organization type (municipality, transit agency, company) and applies symmetrically to all relevant items, energy included.
method.p5: Residual value: geometric depreciation per technology, with a floor; infrastructure is paid when the vehicles using it arrive.
method.p6: Two views: economic (NPV, cost per tonne avoided) and budget (cash out per year, for capital planning).
method.p7: Reproducibility: each result carries the engine version and the input fingerprint; the full methodology is appended to reports.

uncertainty.title: Uncertainty and stress test
uncertainty.p1: The stress test reruns the full engine at the bounds of each assumption’s SOURCED range — never an arbitrary ±.
uncertainty.p2: Three scenarios (conservative, central, favourable) and a tornado of the most influential parameters.
uncertainty.p3: The risk level is computed: does the strategy still win in the conservative scenario?

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.p1: Priority: your data (prices paid, grid-connection quote, subsidies confirmed with the document reference) replaces the registry and is flagged “client data” in reports.
data.p2: Registry: each assumption has a value, a range, an official source, a date and an honest status — “verified” only if the source was actually read.
data.p3: Diesel price: average of the last 12 published months, updated by an archived weekly collection; a change of more than 20% waits for human validation.
data.p4: Consumption: actual (entered or telematics) when known, otherwise the category default flagged “estimate”.
data.p5: Telematics never changes My fleet automatically; vehicles are imported explicitly from the Telematics page, matched against existing units.

infrastructure.title: Charging infrastructure
infrastructure.p1: Minimal sizing per depot: one charger per zero-emission vehicle, of the type suited to its category.
infrastructure.p2: Chargers are commissioned in the replacement year of the vehicles using them (year-by-year phasing).
infrastructure.p3: Power demand shown as a range, taken from the registry assumptions.
infrastructure.p4: A grid-connection quote entered in the project replaces the registry estimate in the total.

subsidies.title: Subsidies
subsidies.p1: A program’s status is COMPUTED from its dates (a program ending before the purchase year is never applied).
subsidies.p2: Caps, bonuses and the public-aid stacking limit are applied by the resolver; an unknown weight class gets the lowest scale, with a warning.
subsidies.p3: An amount confirmed by document (award letter) replaces the computed subsidy of the same program.
subsidies.p4: Application tracking (to prepare, submitted, awarded, received) links each deadline to the plan task or the program end date.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Because their official source has not yet been read and archived. The URL to check is shown in the Library; reports that depend on them say so.
faq.q2: How do I change the discount rate or horizon?
faq.a2: They are project parameters: used by every step and shown in the report appendix.
faq.q3: I don’t know my vehicles’ consumption.
faq.a3: The engine uses the category default, flagged “estimate”. Enter actual consumption in My fleet or import it through telematics to refine it.
faq.q4: My results changed since the last report.
faq.a4: A report is frozen when generated. If data changed since (collected prices, fleet, subsidies), the Reports step says so with the before/after NPV difference.
faq.q5: I have a quote or an award letter.
faq.a5: Enter the grid-connection quote in “Client data” (Organization or Feasibility) and the confirmed subsidy in the Financing step: they replace the estimates.

sections.title: 2. Information collected
paras: We collect only what the Service needs:
items: account: name, email address, organization, role in the organization;
team invitations: email address of the invited person;
fleet and project data entered or imported (vehicles, depots, plans) — essentially organizational data; a unit number or VIN does not normally identify a person;
if you connect a telematics platform: the access credentials you provide and the vehicle data sent by that platform;
technical data needed to sign in (authentication session kept in your browser, the host's technical logs).

sections.title: 3. Purposes
paras: This information is used to create and secure your account, provide the calculations and reports you request, enable collaboration within your organization and answer your requests. It is neither sold nor used for advertising. The Service uses no audience-measurement tool and no advertising cookie.

sections.title: 4. Consent
paras: You consent to this processing by creating your account. You may withdraw your consent at any time by requesting the deletion of your account; some features will then no longer be available.

sections.title: 5. Disclosure and hosting
paras: Information is hosted by Supabase (database and authentication); the website is served by GitHub Pages. The following services receive data only if enabled: email delivery (SendGrid), artificial-intelligence assistant, maps (Mapbox), telematics platforms you connect.
Database hosting region: [to be confirmed]. When information is communicated outside Québec, the Operator first carries out the privacy impact assessment required by law [to be completed].

Artificial intelligence features (optional): when an administrator of your organization enables them, questions asked to the copilot and the project data needed for the calculation (units, categories, mileage, years, garages — never employees' personal data) are sent to Anthropic, PBC (United States), provider of the Claude model, to produce the answer. Only the number of tokens used is logged; the copilot history is kept in the project and can be deleted by its author or an administrator. Invoice and quote reading (if enabled): only the document's text is sent when it has one (otherwise the file); documents may contain billing information (service address, account number), which is not kept in the extracted values, and the document stays in your organization's private storage. Smart import: only headers and a few sample values are sent, never personal-data columns. Privacy impact assessment of this communication outside Québec: [to be completed — to be validated by a lawyer].

sections.title: 6. Retention
paras: Information is kept while the account is active, then deleted or anonymized within [to be confirmed] after the account is closed, subject to legal retention obligations.

sections.title: 7. Security
paras: Exchanges are encrypted (HTTPS). Access to data is partitioned by organization at the database level (row-level security rules) and checked on every request. Stronger encryption of stored telematics credentials is being implemented.

sections.title: 8. Your rights

Write to the person in charge (section 1); you will receive an answer within 30 days. You may also contact Québec's Commission d'accès à l'information.

sections.title: 9. Confidentiality incidents
paras: Every confidentiality incident is recorded in a register. If it presents a risk of serious injury, the Commission d'accès à l'information and the persons concerned are notified promptly.

sections.title: 10. Changes
